content: Two competing patterns for tenant identification in RLS: (1) auth.uid() directly as/mapped 1:1 to client_id -- simplest, but assumes exactly one user per tenant, breaks the moment a client needs a second login. (2) junction table (e.g. client_users or organization_members with user_id + client_id + role) queried via subquery in the policy -- supports N users per tenant, is the recommended default for any real multi-tenant SaaS. Must wrap the junction-table subquery in a SECURITY DEFINER function to avoid infinite recursion if the junction table itself has RLS enabled. Alternative optimization: cache client_id in the user's auth.jwt() app_metadata via a custom access token hook to avoid a subquery per request, at the cost of needing to force session refresh when tenant membership changes.
